1) open-ended and multiple choice questions measure different constructs, 2) open-ended questions are more sensitive to the effects of prior knowledge and 3) open-ended questions can be used to measure the quality of self explanations.
the open-ended questions were correlated with self-explanations and the multiple-choice questions were correlated with prior knowledge.

the quality of self-generated text explanations is correlated with open-ended question performance but not multiple-choice question performance, and that multiple-choice question performance is correlated with prior knowledge about the topic but not with open-ended question or self-explanation quality.

how readers comprehend text.
the question of whether or not multiple-choice and open ended questions are equally valid measures of comprehension.
the nature of text processing and comprehension.

multiple-choice questions are more sensitive to prior knowledge, and open-ended questions are more sensitive than multiple-choice questions to the quality of comprehension processes.

the use of multiple choice questions in reading comprehension assessment may be limited.
